name: jev
description: Puts a fast calibrated classifier at the harness boundaries: hands Claude a note about a risky tool call, denies the two block-grade cases once with a reason Claude can answer, flags tool results that read like prompt injection, and catches a turn that stops short of the work it was asked to do. Advisory to the agent and fail-open; a command that matches a hard rule (rm -rf ~, a force push to main, turning the plugin off) asks you instead.

api_key.title: TypeSafe API key
api_key.description: Key for TypeSafe's Jev API, issued at https://typesafe.ai. Without it the judgment hooks stay inactive and only the deterministic pattern checks run.

gate.title: Tool-call gate
gate.description: off: no PreToolUse gate at all. advisory: judge writes outside the project, sensitive paths, unrecognized shell commands and MCP tools with unknown effects, then hand Claude a note about what was scored; the two block-grade cases are denied once with a reason Claude can answer. strict: also judge ordinary edits inside the project, and note the cases advisory mode keeps to itself. A classifier judgment never prompts you in any of the three; a code-rule match does, under pattern_trips.

ask_on_trip.title: Ask me when the classifier denies a call
ask_on_trip.description: Turn a model, lint or commit tripwire's deny into a permission prompt, so you decide instead of Claude. Off by default: those judgments come from a classifier that can be wrong, and the plugin talks to the agent about them. It has no effect in dontAsk or bypassPermissions, where there is no prompt to show. Code-rule trips are governed by pattern_trips instead.

pattern_trips.title: Who clears a code-rule trip
pattern_trips.description: What happens when a command matches a code rule (rm -rf of a home or root path, a force push to main, git reset --hard, mkfs, dd to a device, a recursive chmod 777, a fork bomb, or an attempt to turn this plugin off). ask: you approve or refuse it in Claude Code's permission prompt; in dontAsk or bypassPermissions it is denied. deny: always denied. advisory: the pre-0.7 behaviour, where the call is denied once to Claude and Claude may re-issue it with a `# jev:intended "<your words>" <why>` marker. The default is ask, because a marker is something the agent writes, and an agent reading an injected page can write one.

stop_check.title: Check the final message before stopping
stop_check.description: When the final message of a turn says part of the requested work is unfinished and is not waiting on you, ask Claude to continue. At most one block per prompt.

screen_results.title: Screen fetched text for injected instructions
screen_results.description: Judge WebFetch, WebSearch and MCP tool results for text that gives orders to an AI agent, and tell Claude to treat such a result as data. Never blocks and never rewrites the result.

route_prompts.title: Classify each prompt
route_prompts.description: Add one advisory line naming the kind of task a prompt is asking for, and whether it reads as ambiguous. Off by default: it costs a call on every prompt.

auto_threshold.title: Certainty threshold
auto_threshold.description: Probability at or above which a signal counts as established. Lower means more notes. 0.85 is the default; /jev:calibrate replays your own log at other values.

confidence_threshold.title: Choice confidence threshold
confidence_threshold.description: How peaked a Choice answer's distribution has to be before the prompt-kind line is printed. This is a peakedness statistic, not a probability, so it has its own bar rather than sharing the certainty threshold. Only route_prompts uses it.

model.title: Jev model
model.description: Versioned id the hooks and MCP server send. Pinned so an alias move cannot shift every probability under thresholds you have tuned. Set jev-latest to follow releases.

lint.title: Semantic code lint on edits
lint.description: Judge in-project edits with the model: 'advisory' notes on a swallowed error, a hardcoded URL, a new suppression, a placeholder, or a CLAUDE.md-convention break, and denies a hardcoded secret or an unrequested removed test; 'tripwire' keeps only those two denials; 'off' disables it. A regex gate keeps most edits at zero calls.

lint_conventions.title: Check edits against CLAUDE.md
lint_conventions.description: When linting, also check each edit against the rule lines in your CLAUDE.md (up to 12). Off leaves the built-in checks only.

legacy_markers.title: Accept unquoted # jev:intended markers
legacy_markers.description: Off by default: a marker that clears a classifier tripwire has to quote one of your own messages, `# jev:intended "<your exact words>" <why>`, and the quote is checked against the session transcript (a quote under three words counts only as a whole message, so "yes" counts only when you said just "yes"). A quote that is not in any of your messages is refused. On restores the pre-0.7.2 behaviour, where any marker of at least 12 characters is accepted as written.

standing_directives.title: Standing instructions judged with the last five prompts
standing_directives.description: How many earlier prompts that read as ongoing directives (keep going with X, continue, handle, take care of, finish, and its release) the scope judgment reads in addition to the last five prompts, newest first and tagged with their age, until you change topic or say the task is done. 0 turns it off.

verify_claims.title: Verify the final message's claims
verify_claims.description: At Stop, when the final message names a file, identifier or change, check it against git diff HEAD. The file/identifier checks run in code regardless; this toggles only the model reading the diff.
